opportunities.name: arXiv paper lookup + Semantic Scholar citation count -> Notes
opportunities.description: For a given topic, subject category and year, run an arXiv Advanced Search by title, take the top result, look up its citation count on Semantic Scholar, and add a '<topic> (<year>): <title> by <first author>, <N> citations' note.
steps: Open arxiv.org and click Search, then go to Advanced Search
Type the topic into Search term with the field set to Title
Tick the subject category checkbox
Select 'Specific year' and type the year
Click Search and open or copy the title of the first result
Open semanticscholar.org, paste the paper title and search
Read the first author and citation count of the matching result
Open Notes, click 'New note' and type '<topic> (<year>): <title> by <first author>, <N> citations'

instances.values: topic=retrieval augmented generation, category=Computer Science, year=2023 -> RIGHT... by Run-Ze Fan, 11 citations
topic=protein structure diffusion, category=Quantitative Biology, year=2024 -> Accelerating Inference in Molecular Diffusion Models... by Ian Dunn, 7 citations
topic=graph neural networks traffic forecasting, category=Computer Science, year=2022 -> Efficient Traffic State Forecasting... by Bin Lei, 1 citation

opportunities.name: Court case + statute lookup -> Notes
opportunities.description: Search CourtListener for a named case, open the Supreme Court opinion to get its citation and decision date, look up a related U.S.C. section on Cornell LII to get its title, and add a note combining them.
steps: Open CourtListener and go to Case Law > Search Case Law
Type the case name and click Search
Open the Supreme Court result and read the U.S. Reports citation and decision date
Open the Cornell LII home page and type the statute (e.g. '18 U.S.C. 2703') into the search box
Read the section title from the first result
Open Notes, click 'New note' and type '<case>: <citation>, decided <date>. See <statute> (<section title>)'

instances.values: case=Carpenter v. United States (585 U.S. 296, June 22, 2018), statute=18 U.S.C. 2703 (Required disclosure of customer communications or records)
case=Bostock v. Clayton County (590 U.S. 644, June 15, 2020), statute=42 U.S.C. 2000e-2 (Unlawful employment practices)
case=Miranda v. Arizona (384 U.S. 436, June 13, 1966), statute=18 U.S.C. 3501 (Admissibility of confessions)

opportunities.name: Peerspace venue search by activity and city
opportunities.description: On Peerspace, enter an event activity and a city, pick the city from the autocomplete list, and click Search to look for venues.
steps: Open the Peerspace home page
Clear the 'What are you planning?' field and type the activity
Pick a suggestion from the activity list if one appears
Clear the 'Where?' field and type the city
Choose the matching city from the autocomplete list
Click Search

instances.values: activity=Team offsite, city=Chicago, IL, USA (several retries; the site showed 'We don't recognize that activity')
activity=Birthday party, city=San Francisco, CA, USA
activity=Product launch, city=New York, NY, USA (the activity was not recognized)

opportunities.name: 1800flowers product search
opportunities.description: Search 1800flowers.com for a type of flower and look at the top result and its price.
steps: Open 1800flowers.com and dismiss the cookie banner if it appears
Click the search box, clear it and type the flower query
Submit the search or pick a suggestion
Look at the first product and note its name and price
